4067abee4a4e3de0.title: Autonomous Laboratories and Foundry Scientific Discovery at the Limit A machine does not discover a mechanism until it creates evidence that could defeat it Core coupling Autonomous experiment x active learning x scientific falsification Research scale 30 linked derivations x 82 chapters x 410 research sections x 200 detailed Research Gates Main result A falsifiable framework for generating, attacking and eliminating process mechanisms rather than confusing recipe optimization with scientific discovery. Series lineage Semiconductor Foundry Technologies x Intelligent Nanomanufacturing - Flagship 20 Publication Abstract This monograph asks whether an autonomous foundry laboratory can do more than optimize an existing recipe. It develops a research architecture in which the system must register competing process mechanisms, identify what its sensors can and cannot distinguish, choose experiments for model discrimination, preserve negative evidence, and issue counterfactual predictions that survive a new tool or fab. Yield improvement, simulation fit, and automation speed are treated as useful engineering outcomes but not as proof of a new mechanism. The central falsifiable proposition is that active experiments chosen to separate rival predictions should reduce the set of observationally equivalent mechanisms and improve preregistered counterfactual forecasts under the same sample, metrology, time, energy, and safety budget as expert DOE and strong safe Bayesian optimization. If the experiment cannot distinguish the models, if failures are selectively forgotten, if the acquisition function exploits a biased proxy, or if cross-tool predictions fail, the scientific claim is narrowed, split, or stopped. Scientific Position and Hard Boundary The work begins with bounded thin-film, deposition, etch, interface, and defect-mechanism challenges in simulation, digital-physical twins, test vehicles, and low-risk equipment states. Autonomous execution is permitted only through typed process intent, equipment capability contracts, explicit authorization, independent metrology, abort logic, and recoverable physical states. No information-gain score may override safety, material irreversibility, chain of custody, environmental obligations, worker protection, or equipment interlocks. Candidate Research Expression Dsci = Delta H of competing models + counterfactual information - sample cost - unsafe risk - hype penalty • Delta H measures reduction in uncertainty over the preregistered mechanism set. • Counterfactual information rewards predictions about interventions or new platforms that were not used for fitting. • Sample cost includes material, metrology, time, energy, and opportunity cost. • Unsafe risk is a hard feasibility concern, not a term that can be purchased by predicted knowledge. • The hype penalty prevents an engineering improvement from being narrated as a causal discovery. Five Layer Research Architecture 01 Competing Mechanism Contract Register rival mechanisms, observable signatures, claim levels, strong baselines, and hard boundaries. 02 Observability and Evidence Graph Map sensors, latent state, calibration ancestry, identifiability, and equivalent model sets. 03 Discriminating Active Experiment Choose controls, interventions, and fidelities for information under sample, energy, and risk budgets. 04 Refutation Memory and Safe Execution Compile typed experiments, preserve failures, detect misspecification, abort safely, and record why models were rejected. 05 Independent Transfer and Successor Choice Demand cross-tool counterfactual predictions, third-party replay, and the right to split, downgrade, or retire a mechanism. Minimum Verifiable Prototype Two process mechanisms are constructed to explain the same historical thin-film or etch observations. Expert DOE, safe Bayesian optimization, and the autonomous discovery policy receive matched samples, metrology, wall time, energy, and safety envelopes. Before the hidden outcomes are revealed, each freezes its hypotheses, predicted signatures, next experiment, acquisition value, uncertainty, and stopping rule. The decisive test is whether independent terminal metrology and a new intervention eliminate or sharply narrow one mechanism, not whether the system merely finds a better recipe. Research Contributions • Separates optimization, prediction, mechanism discrimination, causal support, and cross-platform scientific claims. • Connects observability, identifiability, Fisher information, Bayesian experimental design, causal intervention, and model criticism. • Treats negative results, failed experiments, calibration ancestry, manual corrections, and eliminated models as first-class scientific records. • Maps thirty distinct derivations to chapter, experiment, and Research Gate corridors. • Provides eighty-two chapters with five research pages per chapter: boundary, identifiability, minimum test, adversarial refutation, and successor route.

9e1d65e84320f2a7.title: Atomic Layer Deposition and Intelligent Nanomaterial Fabrication at the Limit English Introduction and Research Abstract This monograph develops a falsifiable research program for using atomic layer deposition to manufacture thin films with predictable electrical, optical, magnetic, mechanical, barrier, catalytic, ferroelectric, or quantum-sensitive functions. Its premise is deliberately stricter than "atomic-scale control is better." A film qualifies only when precursor delivery, surface reaction, composition, structure, and terminal function are connected through traceable evidence on blind batches. Scientific position The core candidate expression is J_ALD = E[L(F*,F)] + β Var(F) + γ B_precursor + ρ P_unsafe. It separates target-function error, functional dispersion, precursor burden, and unsafe probability. All variables, units, normalizations, uncertainty models, and domains must be preregistered. Safety, rights, irreversible harm, missing primary evidence, and terminal functional degradation are hard vetoes outside the weighted objective. Architecture and contents The book contains a scientific-boundary statement, a five-layer architecture, a reading guide, thirty distinct formula derivations, eighty-two chapters with five research sections each, two hundred Research Gates, thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos, and two hundred thirty-three Easter-Egg Equations. Every chapter moves from claim and mechanism to experiment, adversarial validation, transfer, and successor use. The single-section-per-page format keeps each decision object visually intact. Layer 01 · Surface and function state: Define substrate termination, precursor identity, target material state, function, and unacceptable impurities. Layer 02 · Synchronized evidence: Align QCM, spectra, temperature, pressure, exhaust, and timing while preserving uncertainty. Layer 03 · Mechanism ensemble: Retain competing kinetic, transport, and surrogate models until a discriminating experiment is run. Layer 04 · Bounded Bayesian action: Choose the next pulse only inside safety, equipment, precursor, and damage limits. Layer 05 · Functional closure and succession: Judge blind-batch function and aging, then require reconstruction on a changed platform. What makes the study testable The minimum prototype combines two substrates, three controlled surface terminations, and a randomized pulse–purge matrix. It holds out complete batches while predicting dielectric, optical, magnetic, or mechanical function. Mature fixed recipes, human design of experiments, and thickness-only feedback are strong comparators. The claim fails when in-situ signals do not predict terminal function, the model exploits batch labels, safety boundaries are crossed, or recalibration costs exceed the fixed recipe. Evidence and DOI strategy DOI-bearing sources anchor ALD surface chemistry, QCM and QMS reaction evidence, XRF and XANES observation, nucleation delay, plasma assistance, machine-learning models, and human–machine process development. Citations support known mechanisms and constraints; they do not convert proposed results into completed experiments. The companion workbook maps DOI records, chapter interfaces, equations, and all Research Gates. Central deliverable The final Phoenix Answer Embryo is the Atomic Film Intelligence Passport: a reconstructable evidence object binding pulses, surface states, in-situ observations, material function, negative cases, and successor decisions. Its deepest criterion is whether a later team can reproduce, refute, fork, or responsibly retire the work without needing the original authors.
